stem:
Nidhi hammers a bar magnet into several small pieces. She hopes one piece will be only a south pole.

What should she expect?

options.text: Every piece still has both a north pole and a south pole.
A very tiny piece broken off the magnet is nonmagnetic and has no poles.
The piece taken from the end she called north has only a north pole.
One of the pieces will be only a south pole with no north pole.

teacher.key_rationale: Magnetic poles always exist in pairs. Breaking a magnet still yields pieces that each have both a north and a south pole, so an isolated single pole cannot be obtained.
